implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's own command independently in this pod against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11: `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait` at the branch head. 5 passed (3.2m), each row's per-second mark-span log printed, matching what the handoff and the PR body quote. The base half of its first proof (4 failed at 88840d35) was not re-run; the implementer's quoted base run stands unchallenged and nothing I measured contradicts it.

failures.criterion: 2. The comment is created and anchored to the selected text; the composer keeps the draft on every error (plan acceptance 2) - and the PR's own Outcome, 'Send attaches the comment to the words that were selected even when something took the mark away'
failures.evidence: A selected phrase that reads twice in the document loses its anchor whenever the re-anchor has to run, and the reader is told something untrue. Red test: packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts, 'a comment on words that read twice keeps the reading its author selected' (commit 134862da). It is the author-offline row with one change - the selected words are 'the lazy dog', which reads twice in the paragraph 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The vet looks at the lazy dog again.' - and the document's text never changes at all. Run `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait`: 5 passed, 2 failed (4.9m); this row fails at `theComment` with 'Expected: 1, Received: 0' - no comment row was ever created. The composer instead shows 'The text you selected was changed or deleted, so this comment has nothing to attach to. Your draft is kept - select the text again to attach it.', measured with the composer's textContent while both readings of those words are still in the document. Mechanism: the tab is away past the TTL, so layer 1 does not keep the mark (by design); on reconnect the editor's tracked range for the mark is no longer usable, so remarkRecordMark falls through to the whole-document reading, finds the words twice and refuses 'gone' (packages/proof-editor/src/record-mark-retype.ts soleOccurrence). The INFRA-512 architect accepted that refusal for 'two readings of the same words with NO tracked position' (comment on sjawhar/legion#2548, 2026-10-30T09:49:42Z), on the premise that the tracked range covers the reader's own case; the measurement above is the issue's own primary case - a long compose whose tab was offline - with no tracked position left, so the premise does not hold there. Control that the row is sound: the implementer's own author-offline row, identical except that its quote reads once, passes in the same run, and an earlier probe in which the mark survived showed the comment landing at character 62 of that paragraph, the second reading, so the row's offset assertion is reachable.

failures.criterion: 2. ... the composer keeps the draft on every error - what the composer tells the reader has to be about what they are writing
failures.evidence: The re-anchor refusal calls an ask and a suggestion 'this comment'. Red test: packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts, 'an ask whose selected text another writer deleted is not called a comment' (commit 134862da). Run `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait`: the row fails at `expect(await composer(page).textContent()).not.toContain('this comment')`, with the Ask composer showing 'AskClose...QuestionWhich dog?...The text you selected was changed or deleted, so this comment has nothing to attach to. Your draft is kept - select the text again to attach it.RetryAsk'. Measured the same on the Suggest composer in a throwaway probe ('SendClose...Replace withthe spanielReasonSay which dog...so this comment has nothing to attach to...'). One constant serves all three kinds: REANCHOR_REFUSAL in packages/dispatch/web/src/features/margin/margin-context.tsx:56, shown for every ComposerKind ('ask' | 'comment' | 'suggestion'). The wording is new in this change - before it the reader saw the server's kind-neutral ANCHOR_MISSING words - so it is this round's to fix, not a pre-existing one. The same constant is also shown for the 'unmarkable' refusal, where the text was neither changed nor deleted; I did not reach that path on the real surface, so it is named here as a read of margin-context.tsx:248-252 and not as a measurement.

verifiedAtThisHead: The implementer's five compose-wait rows, re-run independently: 5 passed (3.2m) at the branch head, in Chromium against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.7.
The ask path of the re-anchor itself works where the quote reads once: an Ask composer whose mark another writer's edit removed sent its ask and the composer closed (throwaway probe, head 7cfe1f0c).

The sweep's own boundary is covered by the Go tests at unit level and I did not find a hole in it by reading: a mark whose author is connected is kept (both `by` spellings), one is swept a TTL after its author's connection goes, one with no author is swept, and another user's presence keeps nobody else's mark (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/marks_test.go).

notes: The red-test commit was first written with the implementer App as its author, inherited from the working-copy commit this session resumed on; I corrected it with `jj metaedit --update-author` before pushing, so 134862da is authored and committed by the review App alone.

No regression: at the base, a long compose lost its anchor for every quote, so the repeated-quote case is a gap in the fix rather than something this change broke. It is reported as a failure because the change's own acceptance and its PR Outcome claim that case.
